name: Chronic Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in African American and Hispanic populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Gilliam Classification Criteria for Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus

criteria.description: Presence of chronic discoid lesions characterized by erythematous, scaly plaques with follicular plugging and atrophy
Skin biopsy showing interface dermatitis with basal cell degeneration and thickening of the basement membrane
Positive lupus band test with granular deposition of IgG and/or IgM at the dermoepidermal junction
Presence of antinuclear antibodies (ANA) with or without anti-Ro/SSA antibodies
No clinical or laboratory evidence of systemic lupus erythematosus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic chronic discoid lesions confirmed by histopathology, with or without positive lupus band test; exclusion of systemic lupus erythematosus
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on clinical presentation and histopathological confirmation; serology may be supportive but is not definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic discoid erythematous plaques with adherent scale and follicular plugging
searchTerms: discoid plaques with scaling and plugged hair follicles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Atrophic scarring with pigmentary changes in affected skin
searchTerms: skin thinning scars with color changes
scars showing skin wasting and discoloration
skin lesions worsen with sun exposure
redness and thickened skin around hair follicles
inflamed hair follicle areas with hyperkeratosis

common.symptomName: Hypopigmentation or hyperpigmentation in healed lesions
searchTerms: light or dark spots in healed skin
skin color changes after lesion healing
small visible blood vessels in skin lesions
inflammation of mouth or other mucosa

rare.notes: Occurs in a minority of patients over time

laboratory: Positive antinuclear antibody (ANA) test in ~50% of cases
Normal systemic inflammatory markers unless systemic involvement
imaging: Not routinely required; imaging may be used to exclude systemic lupus complications
genetic: Associations with HLA-DR3 and HLA-DR2 alleles
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating interface dermatitis and basement membrane thickening
Direct immunofluorescence showing lupus band at dermoepidermal junction

distinguishingFeatures: Less frequent scarring and follicular plugging
Well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale
Absence of follicular plugging and interface dermatitis on biopsy

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with systemic symptoms
Development of systemic lupus erythematosus features (e.g., nephritis, arthritis)
Non-healing ulceration or secondary infection of lesions
references: Gilliam JN, Sontheimer RD. Skin manifestations of lupus erythematosus. Semin Arthritis Rheum. 1981;11(2):83-124.
Werth VP. Clinical manifestations of cutaneous lupus erythematosus. Autoimmunity. 2005;38(1):1-8.
Kuhn A, Landmann A, Ruzicka T. Cutaneous lupus erythematosus: update of therapeutic options part I. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2011;65(6):e179-93.
